contexts.english: Her body begins to move, her death ever more certain.

findings.description: Zouken's theatrical claim that he must die for Shinji becomes a promise to risk himself. The family obligation remains, but the announced sacrifice is less absolute.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken theatrically announces that he must die, then says he must save his blood relative even at the cost of his own body.
findings.explanation: Zouken's theatrical claim that he must die for Shinji becomes a promise to risk himself. The family obligation remains, but the announced sacrifice is less absolute.

contexts.japanese: 「さて、となるとワシは死ななくてはなるまい。あのようなものでも血縁でな、この身に代えても命だけは救わねばならぬ。カカ、まっこと肉親の情とは命取りよ」
contexts.english: "Still, I can't simply let him die. He is still my flesh and blood, as sad as that is. I will risk myself to preserve his life, at least. Haha. Family love truly is a matter of life and death."

findings.description: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou supposes she judged there was no need to pursue Shinji now that he was no longer a Master.
findings.explanation: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.

contexts.japanese: マスターでなくなった慎二を追う必要はない、と考えてくれたのだろう。
contexts.english: She's probably decided—for my sake—that Shinji isn't worth pursuing now that he's no longer a Master.

findings.description: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken says he learned the Grail would appear and had his grandson contract in his place. He then addresses Shirou as someone belonging to a magical lineage.
findings.explanation: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯が現れると知り、ワシではなく孫にサーヴァントと契約させたのだ。おぬしとて魔道を究める血の末席。
contexts.english: When he learned of the Holy Grail, he—not I—made a contract with a Servant. Like you, he is the last of a line walking the ways of the wise.

findings.description: Zouken's account of sending Sakura to another family becomes an account of the Matous adopting someone. The stated obstacle also changes from the prospective adoptee's lack of circuits to the family's lack of circuits to pass on.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken says the unselected sibling could have been sent out for adoption, but no receiving family would want someone without circuits. The surrounding questions identify Sakura as the person under discussion.
findings.explanation: Zouken's account of sending Sakura to another family becomes an account of the Matous adopting someone. The stated obstacle also changes from the prospective adoptee's lack of circuits to the family's lack of circuits to pass on.

contexts.japanese: 兄妹など最たるものだ。後継ぎは二人もいらぬ。間桐の名が廃れていなければ養子にでも出したのだが、魔術回路がないのでは貰い手などおるまい」
contexts.english: That's doubly so for siblings. There is no need for two heirs. If the Matou name hadn't declined, then we might have been able to adopt someone, but we don't have any Magic Circuits to pass on to begin with."

findings.description: An inborn-inferiority obsession becomes something Shinji was taught.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken says Shinji grew up simultaneously arrogant that he was chosen and compulsively convinced he was inferior by birth.
findings.explanation: An inborn-inferiority obsession becomes something Shinji was taught.

contexts.japanese: 「……まったく、だというのに何処で秘伝を紐解いたのか。アレは選ばれた人間などという驕りを持ちながら、同時に生まれつき劣っているという強迫観念を持って育ちおった。
contexts.english: "...By jove, where did he even learn of such secrets? His head is filled with conceits of being a chosen one, even as he grapples with the inferiority complex of being taught how flawed he was from birth.

findings.description: Kirei taking care of Shirou becomes Shirou owing him.
findings.sourceReading: Despite appearances, Shirou says Kirei ended up fussing over him or looking after him in one way or another.
findings.explanation: Kirei taking care of Shirou becomes Shirou owing him.

contexts.japanese: なんだかんだって世話やかれちまった」
contexts.english: I feel like I owe him now."

findings.description: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.
findings.sourceReading: Saber warns that even slight carelessness could cause last night's near-fatal situation to recur.
findings.explanation: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.

contexts.japanese: 「それで、何をされたのですかシロウ……！　貴方の傷はまだ完治してはいない。少しの油断で昨夜の繰り返しになるのだと、貴方自身も判っている筈です……！」
contexts.english: "What did he do to you, Shirou!? Your wounds aren't fully healed yet. You know what will happen if you're reckless enough to repeat what happened last night!"

findings.description: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Patrolling on foot is like hoping for coincidence, although Saber calls the method dangerous but reliable.
findings.explanation: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 偶然に期待するようなものだが、セイバー曰く『危険ではあるが確実』な手なのだそうだ。
contexts.english: It just happened to seem like a good idea to me, but Saber said that it was a "risky but certain" choice.

findings.description: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.
findings.sourceReading: Because lunch was only leftovers, Shirou urges Saber to eat a proper evening meal before sleeping.
findings.explanation: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.

contexts.japanese: 「魔力の温存は判ったよ。けど人間食事も大切だろ。昼は余りもので済ませちまったから、夕飯はちゃんと食べてくれ。寝るのはその後でいいじゃないか」
contexts.english: "I know you need to save energy, but meals are important, too. I still have some leftovers from lunch, so let me fix you dinner. You can go to bed after that."

findings.description: People with no recourse but to cling to the Grail become people close to it.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou concludes that people who can only cling to something like the Grail are the ones who become Masters.
findings.explanation: People with no recourse but to cling to the Grail become people close to it.

contexts.japanese: いや、もとより“聖杯”なんてものに縋るしかない人間がマスターになる。
contexts.english: In fact, people close to the grail itself are bound to become Masters.

findings.description: Kiritsugu making Grail-dependent people his enemies becomes merely defying the Grail.
findings.sourceReading: Kiritsugu turned those beings or people who could only be saved by the Grail against himself and destroyed it.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu making Grail-dependent people his enemies becomes merely defying the Grail.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣はそれを敵に回して、聖杯を破壊した。
contexts.english: My old man defied the grail and chose to destroy it instead.

findings.description: A war likened to ordinary human life becomes something common within that same war.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei says this killing contest is merely a common event and needs no special status, then calls it crystallized daily life and happiness.
findings.explanation: A war likened to ordinary human life becomes something common within that same war.

contexts.japanese: そう、特別視する必要などない。この戦いはよくある出来事にすぎないのだよ。
contexts.english: It isn't anything extraordinary. It's quite a common circumstance in this war, actually.

findings.description: The Grail eliminating futile labor becomes shortening necessary effort.
findings.sourceReading: The Grail simply removes the accumulated futile labor that people call life.
findings.explanation: The Grail eliminating futile labor becomes shortening necessary effort.

contexts.japanese: —聖杯とは、単にその徒労を無くすだけのもの。
contexts.english: The Holy Grail simply abridges that necessary effort.

findings.description: Saber looking nothing like her prior self becomes looking similar yet different.
findings.sourceReading: Her present indignant display is utterly unlike the gentle expression moments earlier, making Shirou smile.
findings.explanation: Saber looking nothing like her prior self becomes looking similar yet different.

contexts.japanese: そんな姿も、さっきまでの姿と似ても似つかなくて頬が緩んでしまう。
contexts.english: Her pouty face looks so similar yet different from the way she's been acting that I can't help but smile.

findings.description: Shirou's goal equaling ancient wishes and requiring opposition becomes respect for others' reasons.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou says protecting people and becoming a champion of justice is not inferior; therefore, even against five-hundred- or thousand-year wishes, he must make them enemies and fight.
findings.explanation: Shirou's goal equaling ancient wishes and requiring opposition becomes respect for others' reasons.

contexts.japanese: それが他の連中に劣っているとは思えない。なら相手が五百年だろうが一千年だろうが、向こうに回して戦わなくちゃいけないと思うんだ」
contexts.english: That doesn't mean I think any less of the others. They all have their own reasons for fighting. Some have been after the Grail for five hundred years or even a thousand."

findings.description: The beauty of a cold, taut winter sky becomes a frozen-lake simile.
findings.sourceReading: The winter stars are cold and tensely clear, and beautiful precisely because of that quality.
findings.explanation: The beauty of a cold, taut winter sky becomes a frozen-lake simile.

contexts.japanese: 冬の星空は冷たく張り詰めて、だからこそ綺麗だった。
contexts.english: The starry winter sky reminds me of a frozen lake. It's so beautiful.

findings.description: Responding to Saber within Shirou's abilities becomes respecting her needs and actions.
findings.sourceReading: Because she cannot choose her Master, Shirou concludes he must answer or live up to Saber as far as he is able.
findings.explanation: Responding to Saber within Shirou's abilities becomes respecting her needs and actions.

contexts.japanese: なら俺は、自分に出来る範囲でセイバーに応えるしかない。
contexts.english: If it's true, I'll need to respect Saber's needs and actions as best I can.

findings.description: Serving under an exchange condition becomes serving for unspecified reasons.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou understands that Heroic Spirits have their own objective and serve Masters as the other side of a bargain.
findings.explanation: Serving under an exchange condition becomes serving for unspecified reasons.

contexts.japanese: 彼らにも目的があるから、交換条件としてマスターに仕えている。
contexts.english: They have their own reasons for serving Masters.

findings.description: Shirou's imagined example of an unacceptable tactic becomes a prediction reported from Kotomine. Saber's reply still rejects the tactic, making the English transition less direct.
findings.sourceReading: Recalling the priest's explanation, Shirou imagines involving uninvolved non-Masters and causing a disaster as examples of the means he fears Saber might use.
findings.explanation: Shirou's imagined example of an unacceptable tactic becomes a prediction reported from Kotomine. Saber's reply still rejects the tactic, making the English transition less direct.

contexts.japanese: マスターでもない無関係の人間を巻き込んで、十年前のあの日のような惨状を起こすような—
contexts.english: He said that people who have nothing to do with Masters would be drawn into the conflict, and the tragedy of ten years ago would be repeated...

findings.description: Alternative routes to Heroic Spirit status become universal combined requirements.
findings.sourceReading: Servants either won fame in their own era or achieved a deed beyond what a human body can accomplish.
findings.explanation: Alternative routes to Heroic Spirit status become universal combined requirements.

contexts.japanese: それぞれが“自分の生きた時代”で名を馳せたか、或いは人の身に余る偉業を成し遂げた者たち。
contexts.english: Each of us made a name for ourselves in our respective time periods; we accomplished some great deed beyond human capabilities.

findings.description: Saber's proud self-assessment is presented as humility.
findings.sourceReading: She openly prides herself that, regarding swordsmanship, no one surpasses her.
findings.explanation: Saber's proud self-assessment is presented as humility.

contexts.japanese: 「はい。属性を複数持つ英霊もいますが、こと剣に関しては私の右に出る者はいない、と自負しています」
contexts.english: "Correct. There may be some Heroic Spirits who possess multiple attributes, but I would say in all humility that there are none better than I with the sword."

findings.description: Kiritsugu's dying statement becomes an intentional bequest to Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Kiritsugu leaves behind the admission that he himself wanted to become such a thing, then quietly ends his life before Shirou.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's dying statement becomes an intentional bequest to Shirou.

contexts.japanese: その彼こそが“そういうモノ”に成りたかったと遺して、自分の前で穏やかに幕を閉じた。
contexts.english: That's who he wanted to be, and he passed his wish on to me before quietly letting the curtain fall.

findings.description: Rin's plan to deter gambling with death becomes a plan to keep Shirou from doing much at all.
findings.sourceReading: Rin hoped that knowing defeat directly meant death would keep Shirou from readily taking such gambles.
findings.explanation: Rin's plan to deter gambling with death becomes a plan to keep Shirou from doing much at all.

contexts.japanese: 「そうよ。負ける事がそのまま死に繋がるって知れば、そう簡単に博打は打たなくなる。衛宮くん、こういう状況でも一人で夜出歩きそうだから。
contexts.english: "Yeah. I figured you wouldn't take risks or really do much if you knew defeat meant death. But it looks like you're the kind of person to go out at night even in a situation like this.

findings.description: The account reaching the present becomes something unconscious Shirou remembers.
findings.sourceReading: Rin carried the still-unconscious Shirou home, and that sequence brings the account to the present.
findings.explanation: The account reaching the present becomes something unconscious Shirou remembers.

contexts.japanese: 傷は治ったものの意識が戻らない俺をここまで運んで、あとは今に至るという訳だとか。
contexts.english: I was still unconscious, so Tohsaka brought me here and the rest was as I remember it.

findings.description: The unfinished bridge to Shirou's paramount concern is closed as a completed ranking of killing.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou says he would prefer to avoid killing each other, and above all—then breaks off before naming his overriding concern.
findings.explanation: The unfinished bridge to Shirou's paramount concern is closed as a completed ranking of killing.

contexts.japanese: 殺し合いは出来れば避けたいし、何より—
contexts.english: More than anything, I want to avoid any killing.

findings.description: Weak Masters choosing to feed people to Servants becomes a necessity.
findings.sourceReading: Rin bluntly says unskilled Masters feed people to their Servants.
findings.explanation: Weak Masters choosing to feed people to Servants becomes a necessity.

contexts.japanese: はっきり言ってしまえばね、実力のないマスターは、サーヴァントに人を食わせるのよ」
contexts.english: Bluntly speaking, inferior Masters have to feed other people to their Servants."

findings.description: Knowing another Master's identity as an offensive advantage becomes one's own exposure.
findings.sourceReading: Conversely, if a Master knows who another Master is, that Master can certainly launch a surprise attack.
findings.explanation: Knowing another Master's identity as an offensive advantage becomes one's own exposure.

contexts.japanese: 逆に誰がマスターかを知っていれば、確実に奇襲ができる。
contexts.english: Conversely, if the other Masters know who you are, you're just asking to be ambushed.

findings.description: A categorical declaration obliging Shirou to hear Rin out becomes a promise to listen.
findings.sourceReading: Having made such a firm declaration as a man, Shirou feels he cannot refuse to hear the problem Rin raises.
findings.explanation: A categorical declaration obliging Shirou to hear Rin out becomes a promise to listen.

contexts.japanese: が、男が断言した以上、聞かない訳にもいかないのだ。
contexts.english: But I promised to listen, so I need to hear her out.

findings.description: Repeated near misses become repeated meetings.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou questions whether today's meeting is coincidence because lately he and Rin have often narrowly missed one another.
findings.explanation: Repeated near misses become repeated meetings.

contexts.japanese: 「けど奇遇か？　ここ最近よくニアミスするだろ。
contexts.english: "But is this really a coincidence? We run into each other almost every day.

findings.description: Visible grief reassuring other people becomes grief being more normal.
findings.sourceReading: Rin says that in such a situation, the people around someone feel safer if that person becomes spectacularly depressed.
findings.explanation: Visible grief reassuring other people becomes grief being more normal.

contexts.japanese: 「だから、わたしはそれが心配だった。ああいう時はね、いっそ派手に落ち込んでくれた方が周りは安心するものなの」
contexts.english: "That's why I was worried that was going to happen. You know, there are times it's more normal to get spectacularly depressed."

findings.description: Not dwelling in memories becomes drowning in them.
findings.sourceReading: Rin concludes that because Shirou has settled the matter, he neither sinks into depression nor immerses himself in memories.
findings.explanation: Not dwelling in memories becomes drowning in them.

contexts.japanese: だから落ち込む事もなく、思い出に浸る事もないってわけ」
contexts.english: So that's why you're not depressed, and you're just going to drown in your memories."

findings.description: Having no choice but to believe becomes merely hoping.
findings.sourceReading: The knight did not truly possess certainty; he could do nothing except force himself to believe the king would recover.
findings.explanation: Having no choice but to believe becomes merely hoping.

contexts.japanese: 否—そう信じるしか、出来なかった。
contexts.english: Or rather...he hopes.

findings.description: Wondering when anger began becomes asking why the fact causes anger.
findings.sourceReading: The knight wonders from what point he came to feel anger at never seeing the king at ease.
findings.explanation: Wondering when anger began becomes asking why the fact causes anger.

contexts.japanese: それに怒りを覚えたのはいつからだろう。
contexts.english: Why does that make him so angry?

findings.description: The unconscious king becomes half-conscious.
findings.sourceReading: Bedivere bows to a king who is no longer conscious and turns back toward the horse; the following narration is surprised that the supposedly unconscious king speaks.
findings.explanation: The unconscious king becomes half-conscious.

contexts.japanese: もはや意識のない王に礼をし、騎士は白馬へとって返す。
contexts.english: The knight bows to his half-conscious king, and returns to his white steed.

findings.description: Uncertain consciousness becomes a life balanced on a blade.
findings.sourceReading: The king's consciousness is not secure; unless Bedivere asks back like this, the king will fall again into darkness.
findings.explanation: Uncertain consciousness becomes a life balanced on a blade.

contexts.japanese: 王の意識は確かではない。こうして聞き返さねば、また闇の中へ落ちるだろう。
contexts.english: The king's life is balanced on the tip of a blade. The darkness will surely take his king if the knight does not respond.

findings.description: Believing an ambiguous claim becomes a contradictory fact statement.
findings.sourceReading: Young Shirou naturally believes words that could be taken either as a joke or as serious truth.
findings.explanation: Believing an ambiguous claim becomes a contradictory fact statement.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page24:1
contexts.japanese: 俺はその、冗談とも本気ともとれない言葉を当たり前のように信じて、
contexts.english: I just accepted his words as fact...I took it neither as a joke or genuine statement.

findings.description: The English supplies a specific promise about where Shirou sleeps and changes his muddled resolve into having learned a lesson. Sakura's enjoyment of waking him is still present.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou sleepily says he will try harder next time without being discouraged by this, leaving the effort unspecified.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a specific promise about where Shirou sleeps and changes his muddled resolve into having learned a lesson. Sakura's enjoyment of waking him is still present.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-00:page40:1
contexts.japanese: けど藤ねえにはたたき起こされるから、桜の方が助かる。……うん、これに懲りずに次は頑張る」
contexts.english: Then again, Fuji-nee is brutal when she's the one waking me up, so I prefer you do it. ...Yep, I've learned my lesson. I'll try not to sleep in here next time."

findings.description: A slightly shortened workout becomes merely enough exercise to feel satisfied.
findings.sourceReading: Because he overslept, Shirou reduces the time spent moving his body by only a token amount.
findings.explanation: A slightly shortened workout becomes merely enough exercise to feel satisfied.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-02:page2:1
contexts.japanese: 今朝は寝坊したんで、気持ち分だけ体を動かす時間を少なくした。
contexts.english: Since I overslept, I decide to work out just enough to satisfy me.

findings.description: Ayako's presumed higher formal rank becomes presumed superior ability. Both versions remain inferential, so the change concerns what is compared rather than a conversion to certainty.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou supposes that Ayako's formal rank is now higher, despite her continuing determination to impress him.
findings.explanation: Ayako's presumed higher formal rank becomes presumed superior ability. Both versions remain inferential, so the change concerns what is compared rather than a conversion to certainty.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-02:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「……はあ。今じゃ美綴のが段位高いだろうに。アレかな、思い出は無敵ってヤツかな。美化されてるのは悪い気分じゃないけど、それも人によりけりって言うか」
contexts.english: "Is that so? She must be better than me by now. You know how memories get glorified. I don't mind the reverence, but I guess that depends on who sees me that way, too."

findings.description: Issei's concern about what would make him a bad friend becomes an admission that he made Shirou late, even though they arrived in time.
findings.sourceReading: Issei says he would fail as a friend if, after requesting help, he also made Shirou late.
findings.explanation: Issei's concern about what would make him a bad friend becomes an admission that he made Shirou late, even though they arrived in time.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page34:1
contexts.japanese: 「ギリギリ間にあったか。すまんな衛宮、また苦労をかけた。頼み事をした上に遅刻させては友人失格だ」
contexts.english: "You made it just in time. Sorry for all the trouble, Emiya. I'm a bad friend for asking a favor from you and making you late for class."

findings.description: Shirou's explicit interest-versus-business correction disappears.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou corrects Shinji: it is not that he lacks interest in the kyudo club, but that as an outsider he has no business casually entering the dojo.
findings.explanation: Shirou's explicit interest-versus-business correction disappears.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page42:1
contexts.japanese: 「興味じゃなくて用だよ。部外者なんだからおいそれと道場に行くの、ヘンだろ。
contexts.english: "I'm not saying that. Just that I'm not involved and all. I'm not a part of the club anymore, so it's not right for me to just drop into the dojo.

findings.description: The escalating Tiger chant's deliberately broken predicates are normalized into slogans.
findings.sourceReading: Students shout that if the teacher does not wake she is Tiger, and that waking would be precisely what makes her Tiger.
findings.explanation: The escalating Tiger chant's deliberately broken predicates are normalized into slogans.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page65:1
contexts.japanese: 「先生、起きないとタイガーです！」
contexts.english: "You need to Tiger up!"

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page65:1
contexts.japanese: 「よーし、起きろ先生！　それでこそタイガーだぜ！」
contexts.english: "Come on, wake up! Time to wake the sleeping tiger!"

findings.description: Taiga ignoring the teacher-student status difference becomes anger directed at either teachers or students.
findings.sourceReading: When Taiga says she will get angry, she follows through regardless of the other person being a student and regardless of her own position as teacher.
findings.explanation: Taiga ignoring the teacher-student status difference becomes anger directed at either teachers or students.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-03:page74:1
contexts.japanese: 藤ねえは怒るといったら怒る人だ。相手が生徒だろうが自分が教師だろうが関係ない。
contexts.english: When Fuji-nee says she gets mad, she gets mad. Doesn't matter if it's with a teacher or a student.

findings.description: A hellish understaffing situation becomes an outbreak of chaos.
findings.sourceReading: Only Shirou, the manager and Neko are present for work needing at least five people; that three-person staffing is the hellish part.
findings.explanation: A hellish understaffing situation becomes an outbreak of chaos.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-05:page8:1
contexts.japanese: で、フタを開けてみれば手伝いにきたアルバイトは俺一人で、あとは店長さんと娘のネコさんだけという地獄ぶりだった。
contexts.english: But I'm the only one who showed up. The only people there for inventory were me, the boss, and Neko, his daughter. All hell broke loose.

findings.description: The one shop that hired Shirou after Kiritsugu died becomes one of several.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou says this was the only place that hired him immediately after Kiritsugu's death.
findings.explanation: The one shop that hired Shirou after Kiritsugu died becomes one of several.

contexts.ref: セイバールート一日目-05:page13:1
contexts.japanese: 「そのぐらいですね。切嗣が亡くなってからすぐに雇ってくれたの、おやじさんのトコだけだったし」
contexts.english: "Something like that. You were one of the only places that hired me soon after my old man died."

findings.description: Shirou's joking speculation about a spy film becomes asserted backstory.
findings.sourceReading: Seeing Taiga hide behind the newspaper, Shirou wonders whether she watched a spy movie the previous night.
findings.explanation: Shirou's joking speculation about a spy film becomes asserted backstory.

counterexamples.explanation: Rin’s safety condition ends when she gets home.

contexts.japanese: 自分の家に戻るまで
contexts.english: until she gets home.

counterexamples.description: Understanding the argument does not imply accepting its method.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou recognizes the rationale then refuses indiscriminate predation.
counterexamples.explanation: Understanding the argument does not imply accepting its method.

contexts.japanese: おまえの言い分は解った
contexts.english: I get your argument.

counterexamples.description: The heartfelt stop becomes the Command Spell restraint.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou’s extended left arm and plea precede Saber identifying the used seal and freezing.
counterexamples.explanation: The heartfelt stop becomes the Command Spell restraint.

contexts.japanese: 令呪という絶対命令権
contexts.english: absolute obedience enforced by the Command Spell

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s seeming release is qualified by obstructing the attack.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Caster orders Rin killed and permits killing the former Master if he interferes.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s seeming release is qualified by obstructing the attack.

contexts.japanese: 邪魔をするようなら
contexts.english: If he gets in the way

counterexamples.description: Resistance follows an actual forced attack and stops it painfully.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber trembles to a stop, withdraws her blade, and Caster is shocked at her resistance.
counterexamples.explanation: Resistance follows an actual forced attack and stops it painfully.

contexts.japanese: 必死に唇を噛みながら剣を引いて
contexts.english: desperately bites her lips and pulls back her sword.

counterexamples.description: Escape acceptance is corrected to having no choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Injured thought initially describes accepting escape, then revises to only being able to accept.
counterexamples.explanation: Escape acceptance is corrected to having no choice.

contexts.japanese: 受け入れるしか、なかった
contexts.english: I have no choice but to accept it.

counterexamples.description: Saving through obeying the plea coexists with losing her through escape.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The final contradiction does not resolve the two senses into a successful rescue.
counterexamples.explanation: Saving through obeying the plea coexists with losing her through escape.

contexts.japanese: 彼女を失うという事だった
contexts.english: means losing her

counterexamples.description: Refusing Caster does not mean refusing cooperation in general.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says the Grail has nothing to do with it and he will not partner with her.
counterexamples.explanation: Refusing Caster does not mean refusing cooperation in general.

contexts.japanese: おまえとは組まないだけ
contexts.english: I just won't cooperate with you.

counterexamples.description: First aid and inability to cure coexist with permission to stop fighting.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She has treated the wound but cannot heal it fully and tells him he need not fight.
counterexamples.explanation: First aid and inability to cure coexist with permission to stop fighting.

contexts.japanese: 士郎はもう戦わなくていい
contexts.english: You don't have to fight anymore

counterexamples.description: The new site is inferior as sacred ground despite suitability.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Asked whether it surpasses the mountain, Caster says it is slightly inferior but suits her.
counterexamples.explanation: The new site is inferior as sacred ground despite suitability.

contexts.japanese: 多少は劣る
contexts.english: It is slightly inferior

counterexamples.description: Rin pushes him away but honors the promise until he quits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her policy keeps the contradiction of discouraging him while refusing unilateral abandonment of their commitment.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin pushes him away but honors the promise until he quits.

contexts.japanese: あいつがまいったって言うまでは終わらせちゃいけない
contexts.english: I can't end it until he says that he gives up.

counterexamples.description: Enemy breakage remains distinct from creator-induced disappearance.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A projected weapon may break; self-negation makes it vanish when belief cannot reconcile reality.
counterexamples.explanation: Enemy breakage remains distinct from creator-induced disappearance.

contexts.japanese: 投影された武器だって破壊される事はある
contexts.english: Even Projected weapons can break.

counterexamples.description: The dinner example retains the reason for making.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou puts the origin/motive before materials and technique, using Rin’s Japanese-food request.
counterexamples.explanation: The dinner example retains the reason for making.

contexts.japanese: 何故それを作る気になったのか
contexts.english: why you decided to make that

counterexamples.description: The proposed alliance ends in separate competition.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Jointly beat the strongest enemy, then return to solo contenders for the Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: The proposed alliance ends in separate competition.

contexts.japanese: その後で一人に戻ればいい
contexts.english: go back to being solo after that.

counterexamples.description: The summoned Grail and its pre-activation vessel remain distinct.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They cannot destroy the Grail once summoned, but can destroy or stop its vessel before activation.
counterexamples.explanation: The summoned Grail and its pre-activation vessel remain distinct.

contexts.japanese: わたしたちに呼び出された聖杯を壊す事はできない。けど、その前に聖杯の器を壊す事はできる
contexts.english: we won't be able to destroy the Grail once it's summoned, but we can destroy the Grail's vessel.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's reason for refusing passive sacrifice remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If going now will likely sacrifice someone, struggling until the last moment is not shameful by comparison.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's reason for refusing passive sacrifice remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: ギリギリまであがく事なんてみっともなくもなんともない
contexts.english: it's not a shame to try to do anything, to struggle until the very last moment.

counterexamples.description: The path remains one-way from Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin can send mana; Shirou cannot return it.
counterexamples.explanation: The path remains one-way from Rin.

contexts.japanese: 基本的にはわたしから士郎への一方通行
contexts.english: It's basically a one-way path from me to you

counterexamples.description: Rin's confident reassurance remains a bluff against a blocked escape.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her thought-command sounds composed, but narration immediately states there is no route out.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's confident reassurance remains a bluff against a blocked escape.

contexts.japanese: それが強がりである事は言うまでもない
contexts.english: needless to say, it is just a bluff.

counterexamples.description: Mana depletion remains paradoxically protective.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The tentacles pause because prey is docile, and Rin has no mana left to mark her as food; detecting poison would trigger them.
counterexamples.explanation: Mana depletion remains paradoxically protective.

contexts.japanese: 獲物が大人しいからこそ停止している
contexts.english: have stopped because their prey is docile.

counterexamples.description: Saving Shinji from the mass remains distinct from failing to escape with him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin has already extracted him alive, then apologizes when she expects they cannot get out.
counterexamples.explanation: Saving Shinji from the mass remains distinct from failing to escape with him.

contexts.japanese: 慎二、助けられ、なかっ—
contexts.english: I couldn't... save Shinji...

counterexamples.description: Saber destroys the Grail herself and recognizes her own error.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The object she sought and expected to save her is destroyed by her own hand.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber destroys the Grail herself and recognizes her own error.

contexts.japanese: それを自らの手で壊し、ようやく、騎士王は自らの過ちに気が付いた
contexts.english: She destroyed it with her own hands, and the King of Knights finally realized her mistake.

counterexamples.description: Attempted bisection is not narrated as completed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou drives in intending to cut him in two, but Gilgamesh barely dodges.
counterexamples.explanation: Attempted bisection is not narrated as completed.

contexts.japanese: 渾身の双剣を紙一重で躱し
contexts.english: barely dodging my twin swords.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's explanation of the void remains explicitly provisional.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not know what it is and can only infer that Grail destruction caused it.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's explanation of the void remains explicitly provisional.

contexts.japanese: これがなんなのかは判らない
contexts.english: I don't know what this is.

counterexamples.description: Gilgamesh explicitly rejects a mutual-suicide motive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He orders Shirou to hold fast as a foothold until he returns.
counterexamples.explanation: Gilgamesh explicitly rejects a mutual-suicide motive.

contexts.japanese: 死ぬつもりなど毛頭ないわ
contexts.english: I have no intention of dying

counterexamples.description: The scene ends with both branches of danger unresolved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If Shirou is pulled in, both fall; if he holds, Gilgamesh returns and kills him.
counterexamples.explanation: The scene ends with both branches of danger unresolved.

contexts.japanese: もし持ち堪えられたとしても、その時はヤツがこの場に戻ってしまう
contexts.english: Even if I hold out, he'll pull himself out then.

counterexamples.description: Gilgamesh does not consent to the joint fall.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He calls Shirou insane as the latter prevents his return.
counterexamples.explanation: Gilgamesh does not consent to the joint fall.

contexts.japanese: 正気か貴様ぁぁああああ
contexts.english: ARE YOU INSANEEEEEE

counterexamples.description: The rescue instruction preserves the exact rightward direction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The voice tells Shirou to dodge right before doing as he pleases.
counterexamples.explanation: The rescue instruction preserves the exact rightward direction.

contexts.japanese: その前に右に避けろ
contexts.english: dodge to the right before that.

counterexamples.description: Archer's tactical inability to stop the pair survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Diverting attention from Lancer would expose Archer's chest, so the gatekeeper must let them pass.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's tactical inability to stop the pair survives.

contexts.japanese: その状態で俺たちに意識をさけば、次の瞬間ランサーに胸を貫かれるだろう
contexts.english: If he gave us attention in such a situation, he would get stabbed in the chest by Lancer the next moment.

counterexamples.description: The text explicitly denies magical manipulation and affirms Kuzuki's free choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kuzuki is not controlled by Caster; he became her Master by his own will.
counterexamples.explanation: The text explicitly denies magical manipulation and affirms Kuzuki's free choice.

contexts.japanese: あいつは自分の意志でキャスターのマスターになっている。
contexts.english: He became Caster's Master of his own free will.

counterexamples.description: The battle's end includes either side losing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Once one side moves, the Caster battle will end whether Shirou and Rin lose or Rin defeats Caster first.
counterexamples.explanation: The battle's end includes either side losing.

contexts.japanese: 俺と遠坂が破れるにしろ、その前に遠坂がキャスターを倒すにしろ
contexts.english: Whether Tohsaka and I get defeated or Tohsaka defeats Caster before that

counterexamples.description: Shirou attacks Caster first and Kuzuki intercepts him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou lunges at the exposed Caster to draw Kuzuki and is predictably blocked.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou attacks Caster first and Kuzuki intercepts him.

contexts.japanese: 俺は無防備になるキャスターへと襲いかかり
contexts.english: I attack the defenseless Caster...

counterexamples.description: Lancer's savage definition of going easy survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He will only forgo the finishing blow if the spear happens to miss Archer's heart and fails to kill instantly.
counterexamples.explanation: Lancer's savage definition of going easy survives.

contexts.japanese: 即死でなかったのならトドメは刺さない
contexts.english: if his spear happens to miss Archer's heart and it does not kill him instantly, then he won't finish him off.

counterexamples.description: The reconnaissance order's contents survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Lancer must fight everyone, not defeat them on first encounter, and return alive; this explains why the second fight is unrestricted.
counterexamples.explanation: The reconnaissance order's contents survive.

contexts.japanese: おまえは全員と戦え。だが倒すな。一度目の相手からは必ず生還しろ
contexts.english: Fight with everyone. But do not defeat them. Survive the battle against someone you are fighting against for the first time no matter what.

counterexamples.description: Full-force blows and lack of true killing intent remain in deliberate tension.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Lancer aimed lethally at neck and heart but recognizes that withholding his Noble Phantasm means he was not truly trying to kill Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: Full-force blows and lack of true killing intent remain in deliberate tension.

contexts.japanese: 確かに、殺す気ではなかったか。
contexts.english: It is certainly true that I wasn't trying to kill him.

counterexamples.description: The fight ends because Lancer's distraction role has become meaningless.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Caster's surveillance stops, so holding Archer here no longer helps Rin; Lancer's job is done.
counterexamples.explanation: The fight ends because Lancer's distraction role has become meaningless.

contexts.japanese: アーチャーを引きつけるという役割は、もはや意味をなさない。
contexts.english: His role to distract Archer is meaningless now.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's failed defensive premise remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His belief that Projection and pure defense could sustain the decoy role is broken by the first strike.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's failed defensive premise remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 防御に徹するのならなんとかなる、なんて思い違いは初撃で砕かれた。
contexts.english: My misunderstanding of being able to manage with just defense and being a decoy until Tohsaka defeats Caster shattered from the first blow.

counterexamples.description: Both emotional and tactical reasons for protecting Shirou survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin cannot allow that death and her plan also depends on Shirou stopping Kuzuki.
counterexamples.explanation: Both emotional and tactical reasons for protecting Shirou survive.

contexts.japanese: 彼にそんな死に方をさせるのは許せないし、そもそもこの作戦の前提は、彼が葛木を止めてくれる
contexts.english: She can't let him die like that, and the premise of this strategy is that he stops Kuzuki.

counterexamples.description: Caster's fatal injury remains Shirou's judgment before an attempted finishing blow.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou judges the unmoving Caster probably fatally wounded; Rin then closes to finish her, before Kuzuki intervenes.
counterexamples.explanation: Caster's fatal injury remains Shirou's judgment before an attempted finishing blow.

contexts.japanese: あの様子では致命傷だろう。
contexts.english: her wound seems fatal.

counterexamples.description: The apparent victory is explicitly overturned by Kuzuki's movement.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin would have won but for Kuzuki's monstrous athletic ability moving from Shirou to Caster.
counterexamples.explanation: The apparent victory is explicitly overturned by Kuzuki's movement.

contexts.japanese: この男の、怪物じみた運動能力さえなかったのなら。
contexts.english: If not for this man's monstrous athleticism.

counterexamples.description: The role of a Guardian at human-caused apocalypse survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Guardians appear when the world faces destruction by human hands, within hellish aftermaths.
counterexamples.explanation: The role of a Guardian at human-caused apocalypse survives.

contexts.japanese: 世界が人の手によって滅びる場合のみ出現する。
contexts.english: They only appear when the world is about to be destroyed by people.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s final betrayal by his sole ideal survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After repeated betrayals, even the one ideal he trusted betrays him at the end.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s final betrayal by his sole ideal survives.

contexts.japanese: 唯一信じた理想にさえ裏切られた。
contexts.english: betrayed by the only thing he believed in, his ideal.

counterexamples.description: Archer states both purposes for holding Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She is bait, but her presence with Shirou would also obstruct Archer’s plan, so he confines her until it ends.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer states both purposes for holding Rin.

contexts.japanese: そこにオマエがいては都合が悪い。
contexts.english: it would be inconvenient if you were with him.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu’s limit is preserved as a problem of whom one sides with.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A hero of justice can save only the people whose side he takes.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu’s limit is preserved as a problem of whom one sides with.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方に救えるのは、味方をした人間だけだ
contexts.english: A hero of justice can only save those he has sided with.

counterexamples.description: Shared origins and the possibility of becoming Archer survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou accepts that they began from the same place and that he may eventually become the same, which is why he refuses Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: Shared origins and the possibility of becoming Archer survive.

contexts.japanese: 同じところから始まって、いずれ自分もああなるとしても
contexts.english: We have the same beginnings, and even if I were to turn out like that

counterexamples.description: The同行 remains mutual noninterference rather than a command contract.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou and Lancer agree not to meddle in one another’s affairs while traveling together.
counterexamples.explanation: The同行 remains mutual noninterference rather than a command contract.

contexts.japanese: 俺たちもアンタに関与しないから、アンタも俺たちには口を出さない
contexts.english: We won't concern ourselves with you, so don't bother us either.

counterexamples.description: The initially “granted” wish is immediately corrected to almost granted.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration first says the wish came true, then corrects itself: one final push remains.
counterexamples.explanation: The initially “granted” wish is immediately corrected to almost granted.

contexts.japanese: いや、あと一押しで叶おうとしている。
contexts.english: No, it is about to be granted.

counterexamples.description: Saber's negative answer correctly attaches to nonintervention, not permission to kill Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She confirms that she will not interfere whatever happens, then separately asks why Archer wants to kill Shirou.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's negative answer correctly attaches to nonintervention, not permission to kill Shirou.

contexts.japanese: ええ、私は手出しをしません。
contexts.english: No. Whatever happens, I will not intervene

counterexamples.description: Rin's refusal to give up remains paired with recognition of impossibility.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She entertains rescue and miracle while knowing they are impossible.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's refusal to give up remains paired with recognition of impossibility.

contexts.japanese: 諦めはしないが、それが不可能だという事も理解している。
contexts.english: She won't give up, but she knows what is and isn't possible.

counterexamples.description: The headache is correctly distinguished from Projection load.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou identifies it as the recurring symptom associated with approaching Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: The headache is correctly distinguished from Projection load.

contexts.japanese: 即座に行った投影魔術の負荷じゃない。
contexts.english: It isn't from the burden of the Projection.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's self-directed need does not erase genuine rescue intent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even if the emotion faced himself, the will to save Shirou and earnest wish that someone survive were real.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's self-directed need does not erase genuine rescue intent.

contexts.japanese: 俺を救おうとする意思も、助かれと願ってくれた真摯さも本当だった。
contexts.english: his will to save me, and the earnestness of wishing for someone to be saved, were all genuine.

counterexamples.description: Physical direction and emotional wandering remain distinguished.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shinji runs along a known route, but without purpose and in a mentally lost state that merits 'wandering.'
counterexamples.explanation: Physical direction and emotional wandering remain distinguished.

contexts.japanese: 実際は確かな道順に基づいて走っているのだが、その心情は迷走に等しい。
contexts.english: He was headed in a concrete direction, to be clear, but his mental state is utterly lost.

counterexamples.description: Rin correctly distinguishes ritual success from post-ritual allocation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her worry concerned balancing energy to Shirou and Saber afterward, not whether the first-time ritual process would fail.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin correctly distinguishes ritual success from post-ritual allocation.

contexts.japanese: 過程じゃなくて、その後の話よ。
contexts.english: Not the process, but the aftermath.

counterexamples.description: Saber keeps the literal order while deviating from Rin's intended timing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She begins after thirty minutes as commanded but aims to arrive roughly five minutes earlier than Rin predicted.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber keeps the literal order while deviating from Rin's intended timing.

contexts.japanese: 凛の指示通り、三十分後に突入した。
contexts.english: She began her assault after thirty minutes, just as Rin commanded.

counterexamples.description: Saber's tactical bind and uncertainty remain intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Spending strength here harms the Gilgamesh fight, but holding back may be impossible, and even full force may not beat Assassin.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's tactical bind and uncertainty remain intact.

contexts.japanese: 全力で戦ったとしても、果たして勝利し得るかどうか。
contexts.english: can she win even if she goes all out against him?

counterexamples.description: A broken vessel is distinguished from a wish-granting Grail.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If the host fails, there is no Grail function—only unknown contents flowing from the opened hole.
counterexamples.explanation: A broken vessel is distinguished from a wish-granting Grail.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯も何もない。
contexts.english: there won't be any Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Assassin deliberately receives Saber's sword rather than missing a parry.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He attacks her weapon, bends his own blade, and uses the contact to reposition her for Tsubame Gaeshi.
counterexamples.explanation: Assassin deliberately receives Saber's sword rather than missing a parry.

contexts.japanese: セイバーの体ではなく、振り下ろされる剣に刀を振り当てた。
contexts.english: not at Saber's body, but at the sword swinging down toward him.

counterexamples.description: Gilgamesh is explicitly firing one weapon at a time for amusement.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A simultaneous volley would be indefensible; he tests Shirou's limit sequentially.
counterexamples.explanation: Gilgamesh is explicitly firing one weapon at a time for amusement.

contexts.japanese: 一本ずつ、こちらの限界を試すように手を抜いている。
contexts.english: only shooting them off one by one, holding back to test my limits.

counterexamples.description: Saber's resolve remains a separate cause beyond intuition.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration corrects its own emphasis: what truly keeps her alive is the decision to trust the flash and commit every ability to the impossible gap.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's resolve remains a separate cause beyond intuition.

contexts.japanese: 彼女を生かしたのはその決意。
contexts.english: What truly kept her alive was her determination.

counterexamples.description: The bent long blade remains the sole physical difference that permits Saber's survival.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Had Assassin's sword not flexed or bent from prior damage, his magical sword would have remained undefeated.
counterexamples.explanation: The bent long blade remains the sole physical difference that permits Saber's survival.

contexts.japanese: それがたわんでいなかったのなら、彼の魔剣は生涯無敵であったろうに。
contexts.english: Had his blade not bent, his magical sword would have surely been invincible.

counterexamples.description: The distinction between a false origin and genuine beauty remains the pivot of Shirou's answer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks whether something must be false and forbidden merely because the feeling did not originate in him.
counterexamples.explanation: The distinction between a false origin and genuine beauty remains the pivot of Shirou's answer.

contexts.japanese: 自分の気持ちではないから、それは偽物なのか。
contexts.english: Is it fake because it's not my own feelings?

counterexamples.description: Shirou acknowledges sacrifice as reality while continuing to seek happiness without harm.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His ideal does not deny the real tradeoff; it refuses to call the painful best available outcome the end of moral aspiration.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou acknowledges sacrifice as reality while continuing to seek happiness without harm.

contexts.japanese: 多くを救う為に傷つけて、それが最善であっても、それでも—誰も傷つかない幸福を求め続ける。
contexts.english: Even if the best outcome is for someone to get hurt in order to save many, I'm still going to seek a version of happiness where nobody gets hurt.

counterexamples.description: Saber is surprised precisely because she believes Shirou's otherwise extraordinary claim.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her trust makes the asserted fact that he can win astonishing rather than dismissible.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber is surprised precisely because she believes Shirou's otherwise extraordinary claim.

contexts.japanese: セイバーは俺の言葉を信じるからこそ、その事実に目を点にしている。
contexts.english: Saber is surprised because she believes what I'm saying.

counterexamples.description: Strengthening and Projection remain by-products of Shirou's one actual magic.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin's explanation returns: those familiar operations arise along the way toward materializing his inner world.
counterexamples.explanation: Strengthening and Projection remain by-products of Shirou's one actual magic.

contexts.japanese: 強化も投影も、その途中で出来ている副産物にすぎないと。
contexts.english: Strengthening and Projection are just by-products of what I actually do.

counterexamples.description: The shed-lock trap and Rin’s self-exposure are preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou falsely claims an outside lock; Rin corrects him with knowledge available only from inspection.
counterexamples.explanation: The shed-lock trap and Rin’s self-exposure are preserved.

contexts.japanese: で、なんでそんなコト知ってるんだ遠坂
contexts.english: So, how do you know that, Tohsaka?

counterexamples.description: Shirou continues mistaking Rin’s Projection discussion for Strengthening.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Their crossed understanding persists until she shouts the correction.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou continues mistaking Rin’s Projection discussion for Strengthening.
